title: What The Drums Know (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 106bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist rhythm family
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The drums are the oldest instrument — they predate the word
They were present at the first decision and the first thing heard
By anything on the planet that could register a beat
The drums were there before the song and they'll be there after it's complete

[Pre-Chorus]
Every piece of music you've ever moved to had a drummer somewhere in it
Even the ones that didn't have a drummer had the spirit of the drumkit

[Chorus]
What do the drums know that I don't know?
They know the heartbeat is the original metronome below
What do the drums know when the groove locks in?
They know that everything else is decoration — and the beat is what was been
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The drum kit is eighteen separate pieces that a single human manages
All at once with hands and feet in various damaged ages
Of rhythm — coordinating four limbs independently
Which is something the human body does for drums specifically

[Bridge]
When my boys were small I let them bang on anything that sounded
And the kitchen pots and the tins and the table were surrounded
By the natural drums of three boys discovering the beat
And I have never improved on that particular treat

[Outro]
Drums know… the heartbeat was the first music… drums know
That's my boy
